I’ve been teaching English for 6 years now, and I’m passionate about helping learners improve on their English language skills to gain more opportunities in their lives. I specialise in general conversation, Exam Preparation and Business English. I have worked with all levels and can tailor the lessons to fit your needs and goals. My focus lately has been teaching university students who are Business majors planning on studying and working abroad. Prior to this I gained extensive experience in general conversational English, covering speaking, listening, grammar, writing and reading comprehension skills. I also have a background in IT, and have taught the subject at the high school level, so if you need help improving your English for work in the IT field, I can help with that as well.

pro_course_detail.title: IELTS Speaking Practice
pro_course_detail.description:
In the IELTS speaking test you must have an 11-14 minute discussion with an examiner.

The test is given in 3 parts:

Part 1: yourself and your family

Part 2 & 3: random topic

In the lesson we will practice for part 1, 2, and 3. I will time you and give you corrections on your grammar, pronunciation, and vocabulary. I will help you give longer answers and express yourself with more fluency.

The scores are given from band 0 to band 9. Since I am not an examiner and don't work for the IELTS exams I can't give you a score for you to know your level but I can help you do your best at the level that you are at.

pro_course_detail.title: TOEFL Speaking Practice
pro_course_detail.description:
The TOEFL speaking section measures your ability to communicate in an academic setting, the 4 questions will resemble real life situations you may encounter inside and outside of school. 

The TOEFL is scored on a scale of 0 to 30.

I will give you some sample questions and will time you on your answers. I will correct any mistakes and give you suggestions to improve your answers. 

I am not an examiner and do not work for TOEFL so I cannot give you a score but I can help you do your best at the level that you are at.

Talking About Your Day – Start by discussing your daily routine. You’ll learn how to describe your activities and add details to keep the conversation going.
Conversation Starters – Practice essential phrases for small talk, like discussing the weather, hobbies, or recent events.
Expressing Opinions – Learn how to share your thoughts and feelings effectively in simple, natural sentences.
Listening Skills – We’ll also work on responding to others’ comments and keeping the conversation flowing.

Warm-Up (10 minutes): We’ll begin by chatting about your day to help you relax and ease into speaking.
Main Practice (30 minutes): We’ll dive into basic conversation topics. I’ll guide you through speaking exercises, offer corrections, and help you expand your answers to sound more natural.
Feedback & Next Steps (10 minutes): I’ll provide feedback on areas to improve and tips for continuing your practice after the lesson.
Why This Lesson?

If you want to feel more comfortable speaking in everyday situations, this lesson will help. We’ll focus on boosting your fluency, improving your vocabulary, and getting you more confident in conversation. No need to worry about mistakes—I’m here to help you speak with ease and confidence!

Join this Basic Conversation lesson to build your speaking skills and gain confidence in day-to-day interactions. Let's get started on your path to fluency!

pro_course_detail.title: The Sound of American English (Accent Reducction)
pro_course_detail.description:
Do you want to master the unique sound of American English? In this course, The Sound of American English, we’ll dive deep into the specific sounds, rhythms, and intonations that define the American accent. Whether you're just beginning or looking to refine your existing skills, this course will help you speak with clarity and confidence, allowing you to sound more natural in conversations.

What You’ll Learn:
Distinct American Sounds: American English has its own set of vowels and consonants that are pronounced differently compared to other accents. We’ll work on these unique sounds, including the "r-colored" vowels, the flat "a," and others, to help you master the authentic American sound.
Rhythm and Intonation: American English is known for its rhythm and melody, with natural rises and falls in speech. You’ll learn to use intonation patterns that native speakers rely on to convey meaning, emotion, and emphasis.
Word Stress and Syllable Emphasis: Pronunciation is also about where you place the stress in a word. We’ll practice how to correctly stress syllables and words, which is key to sounding fluent and avoiding misunderstandings.
Common American Pronunciation Patterns: Many words in American English are shortened or connected in casual speech. We’ll explore these patterns, such as word linking and reductions (e.g., "gonna," "wanna"), to make your pronunciation more conversational and less formal.
Accent Reduction Techniques: If you’re looking to reduce your accent and adopt a more American sound, we’ll focus on techniques to help you speak more like a native. From practicing subtle changes in vowel and consonant sounds to perfecting rhythm and tone, you’ll learn how to sound more natural in American English.
Listening and Mimicking: A key part of learning pronunciation is listening to how native speakers talk.

Do you understand English better than you speak it? If so, you're not alone. One of the most common frustrations of even the most advanced English students is that they understand what they read and hear, but struggle to express themselves in spoken exchanges. Why? The answer is simple: language learners have more opportunities to read and listen to the language they’re learning than to speak or write it. However, the only way to improve your speaking skills is through practice, ideally with a native speaker. This is especially true of English, because fluency in English depends to a great degree on its peculiar patterns of stress and intonation.

In these lessons, you will get the practice you need to increase your fluency and reach your other English-related goals. We will get to know one another in a relaxed conversation about ourselves and about topics that interest you. I will provide prompts to help you if you’re not sure what you feel like talking about during the lesson. I will also provide constructive feedback and guidance, based on areas in which you have the most room for improvement. At the end of the lesson, you will have access to a feedback document that contains my notes on any errors you made and ways you can improve. This document can serve as a guide for the practice and study you do on your own, outside of lessons.
